metadata.note: The Perkiomen Railroad (Reading's Perkiomen Branch) ran 38.1 miles up the Perkiomen Creek valley from Perkiomen Junction on the Reading main line at Oaks, via Collegeville, Schwenksville, Green Lane, Pennsburg and East Greenville, through the Dillinger Tunnel to Emmaus Junction on the Reading's East Penn Branch; from 1875 its trains ran through to Allentown, a second Philadelphia - Allentown route competing with the North Penn. It opened in five stages (1868 Skippack, 1869 Schwenksville, 1871/72 Green Lane, 1873/74 Pennsburg, Sept 1875 Emmaus Junction) and lost passenger service as a whole on July 15 1955, so it is drawn as five features, one per opening stage, each from its first CONFIRMED year to 1955. One operator throughout - the Philadelphia and Reading / Reading Company - so no ownership split (see ownership_split). Emmaus Junction - Allentown is East Penn Branch track and is NOT drawn here. Research report: research/branches/perkiomen_railroad.txt.

metadata.ownership_split: None. The P&R reported the Perkiomen leased to and worked by it by Nov 1869 (CA-1870), its 1868 trains already appear in the P&R's own timetable ad (CA-1868) and it financed construction (CA-1869a); the 1924 Reading Company reorganisation and the 1945 corporate merger (WP-PA) did not change who ran the trains. If a source shows the Perkiomen company crewed its own trains in 1868-69, split the first feature at the lease date.
not_yet_sourced: Who ran the Aug 1868 - 1869 trains, and the date of the P&R lease (reported done by Nov 1869, CA-1870). Best next source: the full P&R annual report for 1869, or the ICC valuation report for the Perkiomen Railroad.
Last-train day: July 15 1955 (TC-2025) vs July 11 1955 (TC-2014), same author; year agreed. A PUC order or a Reading notice would settle it.
Exact opening of Schwenksville - Green Lane (between June 1871 and Aug 1872; drawn from 1872) and of Green Lane - Pennsburg (between June 1873 and Jan 1874; drawn from 1874).
'Perkiomen and Reading' / 'Perkiomen-Reading Railroad' (TC-2014): no primary source names such a company; probably a reorganisation of the corporate shell, not a change of operator.

Service level 1876-1955: no 20th-century timetable was read; the 1951/52 Official Guide Table 19 survives in OCR with only one time column, and some of its columns were Schuylkill Valley Transit buses (Norristown - East Greenville). All headways after 1875 are estimates.
Commuter character of the lower end (Oaks, Collegeville) is unsourced; tagged intercity_rail.
Skippack station's exact site: the Skippack/Schwenksville cut is at Fowler milepost 10.0 measured along the trace, not at a located station.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn: every section ends with passenger service in 1955. Post-1955 freight (to the mid-1960s on the upper valley, Collegeville - Green Lane abandoned 1973, Pennsburg - Emmaus still East Penn Railroad freight), the Graterford prison spur and the Colebrookdale Branch are not drawn.

Perkiomen Junction - Arcola (trace mi 0.0 - ~4.8) follows OpenHistoricalMap's untagged railway way, i.e. OHM's reconstruction of the grade, not an OSM-mapped roadbed; from Arcola north it is the OSM Reading-tagged abandoned grade under the Perkiomen Trail. segments.note: First section of the Perkiomen Railroad, Perkiomen Junction (on the Reading main line at Oaks) to Skippack, 10 miles, opened for traffic in August 1868 (CA-1869a, P&R annual report). The Dec 1868 P&R timetable ad shows passenger trains, returning from Skippack at 8.10 a.m. and 1.25 p.m. and connecting with Reading trains (CA-1868); April 1869 ad: Skippack passengers take the 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. trains from Philadelphia, with stage lines meeting trains at Collegeville and Skippack (CA-1869b). Skippack was the terminal until Oct/Nov 1869 (CA-1869c). Steam from the start - no animal-power years. Operator: these 1868 trains appear inside the P&R's own timetable advertisement and the P&R financed construction (CA-1869a), and the P&R reported the road leased to and worked by it by Nov 1869 (CA-1870); who crewed the Aug 1868 - 1869 trains is not established (see metadata.not_yet_sourced), so the feature carries the Reading colour throughout. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from 2 round trips a day in the Dec 1868 and April 1869 ads.
sources: Segment-level: 1868 start from CA-1869a (opened August 1868 to Skippack) and CA-1868 (passenger trains in the Dec 1868 P&R timetable ad); service confirmed by CA-1869b and CA-1869c; the 1869 end is the start of the Schwenksville extension (CA-1869d), not a break in service. Headway is an estimate from those ads.

segments.note: From Sept 27 1875 the Perkiomen was a through route: the extension to Emmaus Junction opened that day (NYT-1875) and the Nov 1 1875 timetable runs Philadelphia - Allentown trains 'via Perkiomen Branch', some with through cars to and from Mauch Chunk (CA-1875). Operated by the Philadelphia and Reading (Reading Company from the 1924 reorganisation - same operator); the Perkiomen Railroad Company was leased to and worked by the P&R by Nov 1869 (CA-1870) and merged into the Reading Company in 1945 (WP-PA), a corporate change only. Passenger service ended with the last train on July 15 1955 (TC-2025, which describes crowds riding through the Dillinger Tunnel to Emmaus and on to Allentown, last run behind diesel 616, 'single coach' trains by then); TC-2014, by the same author, says July 11 1955 - day conflict recorded, the year is 1955 either way. The whole line closed to passengers together; there was no cut-back of the upper end. Freight continued after 1955 (context only, not drawn): 'until the mid-1960s' on the upper valley, Collegeville - Green Lane abandoned 1973 (TC-2025), Pennsburg - Emmaus still worked today by the East Penn Railroad as freight. headway_min is an ESTIMATE: the Nov 1 1875 P&R timetable (CA-1875) shows 3 Philadelphia - Allentown through trains each way via the Perkiomen plus a Sunday train; no 20th-century timetable was read (the Feb 1952 Official Guide's Table 19 'Perkiomen Junction and Allentown' survives in OCR with only one time column), so the figure is carried forward unverified to 1955.
sources: Segment-level: 1875 start from NYT-1875 (extension and first through passenger train Sept 27 1875) and CA-1875 (Nov 1 1875 timetable); 1955 end from TC-2025 (last train July 15 1955) with TC-2014 (July 11 1955) as a conflicting day in the same year; Pennsburg, East Greenville and Emmaus listed without a freight-only mark in the 1951/52 Official Guide index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, Table 19).
